name: Roll call
chair_script: Good morning, delegates, and welcome to the {committee}. The chair will now call the roll. When you hear your delegation's name, raise your placard and answer "present" or "present and voting". A delegation that is present and voting may not abstain on substantive votes.
chair_next: Call each delegation, or let students answer on their devices. Delegations with no student are answered by the engine and marked computed. When the roll is complete, announce how many are present and the majority needed, then move to setting the agenda.
student_prompt: Answer the roll for your delegation: Present, or Present and voting. If you choose Present and voting you can't abstain on the resolution.

name: Setting the agenda
chair_script: With {present} delegations present, a simple majority is {majority}. The floor is open for a motion to set the agenda. Is there a motion to set the agenda to {agenda}? Is there a second? Are there any objections? Seeing none, the agenda is set.
chair_next: Type the agenda topic. With one topic, set it by consent; with two, take a motion and vote. Then open the general speakers list.
student_prompt: Listen for the motion to set the agenda. You can second it, or ask to speak for or against it.

name: Opening statements
chair_script: The chair now opens the general speakers list on {agenda}. Each delegation will deliver its opening statement. Speaking time is {speaking_time} seconds. Delegates who finish early may yield their time to the chair, to questions, or to another delegate.
chair_next: Students add themselves to the list from the Floor tab, or you add them. Call each speaker, start the timer and handle yields. When every delegation has spoken, or the list runs out, open the floor.
student_prompt: Add yourself to the speakers list and deliver your opening statement out loud. Your draft is in the My speech tab; it's only for you.

name: Debate: the floor
chair_script: The floor is open. Are there any points or motions on the floor?
chair_next: Take motions in order of precedence, the most disruptive first: suspend, close debate, unmoderated caucus (up to 10 minutes), moderated caucus, introduce an amendment that has its signatories. With no motion, the general speakers list continues. Closing debate needs two-thirds of those voting; then go to voting procedure.
student_prompt: Speak, lobby and negotiate. Use the tabs to join the speakers list, raise a point, propose or vote on motions, message other delegates, draft amendments and keep your friends and foes sheet up to date.

name: Voting procedure
chair_script: Debate is closed. We are now in voting procedure. The doors are closed: there is no talking and no passing of notes; delegates may raise only points of order. We will vote first on any amendment on the floor, then on {target}. A simple majority of those present and voting is required.
chair_next: Take any motion to divide the question or to vote by roll call. Start a whip count if you want one, then open the vote. If the resolution fails and another draft is ready, reopen the floor with it; otherwise go to the debrief.
student_prompt: No talking. Predict the vote if there is a whip count, then vote for your delegation.

name: Results and debrief
chair_script: With {yes} in favour, {no} against and {abstain} abstentions, the {target_short} {result}. The chair thanks all delegates. Let's look at how well we read the room.
chair_next: Show the debrief: each student's whip accuracy against the votes actually cast, how the prediction engine did on this vote, and which delegations decided the result.
student_prompt: Read your debrief: how many delegations you predicted correctly, which votes decided the result, and how your own vote matched your country's mandate.

student_prompt: Answer the roll for your Council member: Present.
